title: 2014 HMMT November Guts Problem 6
statement:
In the octagon COMPUTER exhibited below, all interior angles are either \(90^{\circ}\) or \(270^{\circ}\) and we have \(C O=O M=M P=P U=U T=T E=1\).

Point \(D\) (not to scale in the diagram) is selected on segment \(R E\) so that polygons COMPUTED and \(C D R\) have the same area. Find \(D R\).

[Diagram omitted from this imported transcription; consult the HMMT archive while reviewing the problem.]

solutions.text: 2 The area of the octagon \(C O M P U T E R\) is equal to 6 . So, the area of \(C D R\) must be 3. So, we have the equation \(\frac{1}{2} * C D * D R=[C D R]=3\). And from \(C D=3\), we have \(D R=2\).
